I need to correct the scrape.yaml port name to match what main already uses, and I'm considering a regression test that checks the two files agree. Since the tests are in Python without a YAML library, I'm weighing a simple regex-based check on the raw text, and I'm looking at whether any existing tests already read the deploy files.

I'm settling on the test's location: I'll put it under tests/io_shop and find the repo root from the file's own path, going up two levels.
The scrape config on main selects `port: metrics`, but the production values now name it `http-metrics`, so I'm fixing the selector and adding a test to keep them in sync.

input.explanation:
The fault (on main, which I read; the running revision c3c36da is not in main's history, so I can't say what it held): `deploy/values-production.yaml` sets `metrics.portName: http-metrics`, but `deploy/scrape.yaml` (the ServiceMonitor) still has `endpoints[].port: metrics`. The ServiceMonitor finds its scrape endpoint by the port's name. A comment in `deploy/scrape.yaml` itself says that a name matching no port is not an error, just an empty target list, and that nothing checks the two names agree. So when the port was renamed, Prometheus had nothing to scrape. Changing the port back would reverse the platform's naming convention, so instead I changed `deploy/scrape.yaml` to select `http-metrics`, the name the values file gives the port.

To stop the two drifting apart again, I added `tests/io_shop/test_scrape_config.py`. It reads both deploy files as text with simple line parsing, so it doesn't depend on a YAML library. It asserts that every `port:` named under the ServiceMonitor's `endpoints` equals `metrics.portName`. Against the code as it stood (`metrics` vs `http-metrics`) that assertion does not hold, and with this change it should. If a rename touches only one of the files in future, this test should fail in the same pull request, instead of the problem showing up as missing samples in production.

# How the platform's Prometheus collects the shop's metrics.
#
# The ServiceMonitor the platform applies with the shop's chart, kept in the
# repository beside how the shop is deployed, so that how it is collected
# changes in the same pull request as what it is collected from.
#
# It selects the shop's Service by label, then the endpoint to scrape on that
# Service by the port's *name* - never its number - so a port can move without
# anything here being touched.
#
# The name here has to be the one `metrics.portName` in values-production.yaml
# gives the port. A name that matches no port is not an error to the operator,
# it is a target list with nothing in it - so tests/io_shop/test_scrape_config.py
# checks that the two agree.
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata:
  name: io-shop
  labels:
    release: prometheus
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: io-shop
  endpoints:
    - port: http-metrics
      path: /metrics
      interval: 15s

input.summary: Point the ServiceMonitor at the renamed `http-metrics` port and add a test that the scrape port name matches metrics.portName
